item: The launcher caps glibc's malloc arenas at 2 (R114), and each session's record, the crash report and the soak window say whether the process ran with the cap
key_paths: scripts/launch.sh; src/monitoring/session_hwm.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; tests/test_malloc_arena_default.py; docs/ledger/RULINGS_INDEX.md
summary: Maintainer answer 16c (2026-10-01): MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 is the default of every instance started with scripts/launch.sh, and the diagnostics must show which instances run with it. The launcher exports it after reading oo.env and only when nothing set it, so an operator's own value is kept; glibc reads it once when the server process starts, so an instance has it from its first launch through the launcher after an update. The reading (session_hwm.allocator_setting) is taken from the environment the process STARTED with (/proc/self/environ), never a later os.environ, and effective is true only on glibc started with a plain positive number: macOS, Alpine and Windows read as not capped, and a value that is not a plain number reads as unknown. It is stamped into each session's record, so a death is read against the setting that session ran with; the crash report prints it beside the heap it qualifies; the soak window's memory-guard block carries the running process's. 988.7 MB freed-but-held of 3,437.3 MB anonymous memory (28.8%) at the 2026-09-30 21:08:38 reading is an upper bound on what the setting could have returned at that moment, not a prediction; the performance cost is not measured before shipping and is read afterwards. Not shown yet, owned elsewhere: the manifest hardware header (bundle.py) and each boot record. Mutation-checked: no default, an unconditional override, os.environ instead of the starting environment, no allocator in the record, the soak window or the report, a non-glibc process counted as capped, and a garbage value counted as applied are each caught.
